title: Correct velocity change
description: Essential: Student must calculate Δv = v_final - v_initial = -1.3 m/s - 1.5 m/s = -2.8 m/s.

title: Correct acceleration
description: Essential: Student must compute a = Δv / Δt = -2.8 m/s / 0.7 s = -4 m/s².

title: Proper sign convention
description: Important: Student must define a consistent direction (e.g., right as positive) and apply it correctly to initial and final velocities.

title: Acceleration definition
description: Important: Student must correctly apply the kinematic definition a = Δv/Δt, not confuse it with average speed formulas.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Student should include proper units (m/s and m/s²) in final answers and show unit analysis in calculations.

title: Sign error in Δv
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly calculates Δv as v_initial - v_final, or ignores signs, yielding +2.8 m/s.

title: Incorrect time usage
description: Pitfall: Student uses the wrong time interval (e.g., time for one-way travel) or misplaces decimal in division.
